data.value: {0}: {1} is there already and may not be replaced ({2}). The file was skipped, the others are copied, the next run tries it again. Either the storage protects written files from change and deletion (WORM on a NAS), or the file belongs to another account and this one may not change it.

data.name: ManifestReplaceRefused
data.value: {0}: {1} of the last run may not be replaced ({2}). A shared folder rewrites it and every changed file at each run; storage that does not let written files change (WORM or protection from deletion on a NAS) needs «A separate folder for each backup»: then files are only added, nothing is replaced.

data.name: FolderRenameRefused
data.value: {0}: a folder with files in it cannot be renamed here (a NAS with WORM does that), so the set is written straight under its own name. It is complete once custos-set.json, written last, is in it.

data.name: StoreNoFolderRename
data.value: A folder with files in it cannot be renamed here (a NAS with WORM does that). Backups in separate folders are written straight under their own names; a backup is complete once custos-set.json is in its folder.

data.name: StoreWormInfo
data.value: WORM: the storage locks a file {1} h after it is written and then does not let it be deleted for {0} days. Backups go into separate folders, straight under their own names; retention deletes an old backup once its protection is over.

data.name: StoreWormLocksAtOnce
data.value: The storage locks a file at once: a file that was just written cannot even get its name ({0}). CUSTOS cannot write backups here. Set a delay before the lock in the WORM settings of the NAS, for example 1 hour or more.

data.name: SetLockedWorm
data.value: Set «{0}» in {1} is protected from deletion until {2} (WORM); retention will delete it after that.

data.name: SetDeleteRefusedWorm
data.value: Could not delete the old set «{0}» in {1}: {2}. By the WORM days of the destination its protection is over; if the NAS keeps files longer, set its days in the destination. The next run tries again.

data.name: WormNeedsSets
data.value: {0}: with WORM a written file cannot be replaced for {1} days, so only backups that are never overwritten can go there: archives or a separate folder for each backup. A mirror and a shared folder replace files.

data.name: WormRetentionTooShort
data.value:
{0}: WORM for {1} days does not let a backup be deleted sooner than {2} after it is written, and this retention would delete backups after {3} already. They would stay until their protection is over anyway, and the destination would hold more backups than set.
{4}

data.name: ObjectLockRetentionTooShort
data.value:
{0}: S3 Object Lock for {1} days does not let a backup be deleted sooner than {2} after it is uploaded, and this retention would delete backups after {3} already. They would stay in the bucket until their protection is over anyway, taking space, and there would be more backups than set.
{4}

data.name: ReadmeIntro
data.value: CUSTOS does not load dumps into a server by itself. When a database is needed back, run the commands below. Run them in cmd, not in PowerShell (PowerShell spoils the input given with «<»), from the folder that holds the folder «db». The programs mysql (mariadb), psql and createdb are in the folder of the server's programs (bin): go there first or write the full path to them. The commands ask for the password of the server's administrator (root, postgres); write another user if yours is different. Load a database into an empty one: tables already there get in the way.
